sections.heading: Is Spray Foam Roofing a Good Idea? Benefits, Disadvantages, and Roof Life

c.v: Is it a good idea to spray foam your roof?

runs.v: On a flat or low-slope roof in sound condition, often yes: the foam adds insulation and waterproofing in one seamless layer, goes over the existing roof without a full replacement, and renews with a recoat instead of a tear-off.

c.v: What are the disadvantages of a foam roof?

runs.v: The foam must be coated to protect it from UV and recoated every 10 to 20 years, spraying needs dry, mild weather and experienced installers to build an even thickness, and a punctured or hail-dented surface needs prompt repairs before leaks reach the foam. For comparison on pitched roofs, asphalt shingles last 20 to 30 years depending on type, metal roofs can last 40 to 80 years with proper installation, and slate roofs have a lifespan of 60 to 150 years, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart.

sections.heading: Spray Foam Roofing vs. Spray Foam Insulation Services

c.v: Spray foam roofing and spray foam insulation services

runs.v: use similar chemistry in different places. Roofing foam goes on top of the roof deck, outside the building, and is coated against the weather; insulation foam is sprayed inside the house, under the roof deck in the attic, in walls, and around pipes, windows, and rim joists, while blown cellulose or fiberglass covers the attic floor. A roof-top foam layer can insulate the whole roof area from above without touching a finished attic room, a garage ceiling, or the living space, and it seals the joints where the roof meets a block parapet, siding, a chimney, or the eave. Insulation types include cellulose, fiberglass, and spray foam, and insulation must be installed after air sealing to be effective; moisture management is essential when converting attics to unvented spaces with SPF under the deck. Interior insulation projects in Bloomfield typically run about $3,500 to $12,500, and PSE&G's home energy program has advertised rebates of up to $7,500 for insulation and air-sealing upgrades, so confirm current terms with the utility.

faqs.q: Can spray foam roofing be applied over my existing roof in Bloomfield?

runs.v: Yes, over a structurally sound, dry EPDM, TPO, modified-bitumen, or BUR roof that carries fewer than 2 covering layers, after core sampling and infrared moisture scanning confirm the substrate; full removal applies once a roof is water-soaked or already carries 2 or more layers, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4.

faqs.q: Does a commercial spray foam roof require a permit in Bloomfield?

runs.v: A commercial, multi-family, or attached building needs a permit when the work recovers or replaces more than 25% of the total roof area in 12 months, under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, while a detached one- or two-family re-roof counts as ordinary maintenance. Confirm the filing with the Township of Bloomfield construction office.

faqs.q: Does a spray foam roof on a Bloomfield historic-district property need extra approval?

runs.v: It can. Confirm with the Township of Bloomfield construction office before work, because properties in a historic district can need extra review; per the National Park Service, National Register listing alone places no federal restriction on a private property owner.

faqs.q: Why does my Bloomfield flat roof need a protective coating over the foam?

runs.v: The polyurethane foam is UV-sensitive and degrades when exposed, so the coating shields it and carries the surface against weather and foot traffic; a recoat every 10 to 20 years, acrylic at 10 to 15 and silicone at 15 to 20, restores that protection, per the SPFA and SPF manufacturers.

faqs.q: How long does a spray foam roof last on a Bloomfield commercial building?

runs.v: Thirty or more years when the protective coating is maintained, per the SPFA and SPF manufacturers, because each recoat restores the UV protection that carries the foam through another cycle.
